AbstractParserHandlingTest#testNoLanguag.spec: RDF 1.1 Concepts section 3.3 (Literals): a literal is a language-tagged string if and only if its datatype IRI is rdf:langString, and then it has a non-empty language tag; RDF 1.2 Concepts section 3.4
AbstractParserHandlingTest#testNoLanguag.note: "G'day mate"^^rdf:langString has no language tag, so it is not a literal of the abstract syntax. RDF4J (RDFLangStringDatatypeHandler) turns it into the xsd:string literal "G'day mate"; core refuses (term.invalid-langtag).

ResolveUriTest#colonInPathWithoutBaseFai.spec: RFC 3986 section 3.1 (scheme = ALPHA *( ALPHA / DIGIT / "+" / "-" / "." ) ":") and section 4.2; RDF 1.2 Turtle section 6.3
ResolveUriTest#colonInPathWithoutBaseFai.note: core.parse('<urn:s> <urn:p> <path/foo:bar> .', {format:'turtle'}) accepts and keeps the relative reference <path/foo:bar> unresolved, while <a/b> with no base is refused. 'path/foo' cannot be a scheme (contains '/'), so the reference is relative and there is no base.

ResolveUriTest#leadingColonInFirstPathSe.spec: RDF 1.2 Turtle section 6.3 (relative IRI references are resolved per RFC 3986); RFC 3986 section 4.2 ("A path segment that contains a colon character (e.g., \"this:that\") cannot be used as the first segment of a relative-path reference"); RFC 3987 section 2.2 irelative-ref / ipath-noscheme
ResolveUriTest#leadingColonInFirstPathSe.note: core.parse('<urn:s> <urn:p> <:foo> .', {format:'turtle', baseIRI:'http://example.org/dir/doc'}) accepts and gives <http://example.org/dir/:foo>. ':foo' is neither an absolute IRI (a scheme starts with ALPHA) nor a relative reference (ipath-noscheme forbids ':' in the first segment), so RFC 3986 5.2 resolution is not defined for it. The same check would refuse <:foo> and <1a:foo> in N-Triples, which core also accepts.

AbstractNQuadsParserUnitTest#testSparqlV.spec: RDF 1.2 N-Quads section 5.3 Grammar, productions [2] statement ::= directive | quad, [3] directive ::= versionDirective, [4] versionDirective ::= 'VERSION' versionSpecifier, [5] versionSpecifier ::= STRING_LITERAL_QUOTE; section 6.1: the version announcement is only a hint (https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf12-n-quads/#sec-grammar)
AbstractNQuadsParserUnitTest#testSparqlV.note: core.parse('VERSION "1.2--basic"', {format: 'nquads12'}) rejects with term.invalid-iri 'expected subject (IRIREF or BLANK_NODE_LABEL) at line 1, column 1'; VERSION "1.2" is rejected the same way, and so is a VERSION line followed by a quad. turtle12 accepts the same directive. Expected: an empty graph.

AbstractNQuadsParserUnitTest#testSparqlV.spec: RDF 1.2 N-Quads section 5.3 Grammar, [5] versionSpecifier ::= STRING_LITERAL_QUOTE (double quotes only; there is no STRING_LITERAL_SINGLE_QUOTE in the N-Quads grammar) (https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf12-n-quads/#sec-grammar)
AbstractNQuadsParserUnitTest#testSparqlV.note: RDF4J accepts VERSION '1.2--basic' in N-Quads; the grammar allows only a double-quoted version specifier, so rejection is correct. Factoidal rejects, but for the reason in the nquads12-version-directive defect (no VERSION support at all); when that is fixed this case must still reject.

AbstractNQuadsParserUnitTest#testDirLang.spec: RDF 1.2 Concepts section 3.4 Literals: 'If and only if the datatype IRI is http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#langString or http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#dirLangString, there is a non-empty language tag' (https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf12-concepts/#section-Graph-Literal)
AbstractNQuadsParserUnitTest#testDirLang.note: "Hello"^^rdf:dirLangString has no language tag and no base direction, so no RDF literal can be built from it. RDF4J (VERIFY_DATATYPE_VALUES=false, its default) silently rewrites it to "Hello"^^xsd:string (RDFParserHelper.createLiteral); Factoidal rejects with term.invalid-langtag.

RDFXMLParserTest#testFatalErrorDoctypeDe.spec: XML 1.0 (Fifth Edition) section 2.8 [22] prolog ::= XMLDecl? Misc* (doctypedecl Misc*)? and section 5.1 (a non-validating processor need not read external parameter entities); RDF 1.2 XML Syntax section 2 (an RDF/XML document is an XML document)
RDFXMLParserTest#testFatalErrorDoctypeDe.note: RDF4J refuses any DOCTYPE by default (XMLParserSettings.DISALLOW_DOCTYPE_DECL=true, an XXE hardening choice). The document is well-formed XML; Factoidal skips the unread external parameter entity and gives the one triple <http://example.org/foo/bar> rdfs:label "Foo Bar".

TriGParserCustomTest#testParseTruePrefix.spec: RDF 1.2 TriG section 4.5 (grammar [PNAME_LN], [PN_PREFIX]) and RDF 1.2 Turtle section 6 note 3: "When tokenizing the input and choosing grammar rules, the longest match is chosen."
TriGParserCustomTest#testParseTruePrefix.note: In object position the lexer reads 'true'/'false' as BooleanLiteral even when ':' follows, so true:o (a PNAME_LN, the longest match) is refused with 'expected . after triple'. Subject and predicate positions accept true:s / true:p; truex:o is accepted. Same in turtle, trig, trig12.

TriGParserCustomTest#testDirLangStringNo.spec: RDF 1.2 Concepts section 3.3 (Literals: the datatype IRI is rdf:dirLangString if and only if the literal has a language tag and a base direction); W3C rdf-tests rdf12 ntriples-langdir-bad-5 is a negative syntax test of the same literal
TriGParserCustomTest#testDirLangStringNo.note: RDF4J (VERIFY_DATATYPE_VALUES=false, its default) rewrites "Hello"^^rdf:dirLangString with no language tag to the xsd:string literal "Hello"; Factoidal refuses it (term.invalid-langtag).

CustomTurtleParserTest#testSES2165Litera.spec: RDF 1.2 Turtle section 6.5 [22] RDFLiteral ::= String (LANG_DIR | ('^^' iri))?; section 6.1 white space separates terminals; section 6.2 comments are treated as white space (RDF 1.1 Turtle section 6.5 [128s] same)
CustomTurtleParserTest#testSES2165Litera.note: core rejects white space or a comment between ^^ and the datatype IRI ("expected prefixed name"); '^^' and iri are separate terminals, so WS/comment between them is allowed. Same in turtle12 and trig.

CustomTurtleParserTest#testParseTruePref.spec: RDF 1.2 Turtle section 6.5 [39] PNAME_NS ::= PN_PREFIX? ':', [58] PN_PREFIX, and Note 3: "When tokenizing the input and choosing grammar rules, the longest match is chosen." (RDF 1.1 Turtle section 6.3 same)
CustomTurtleParserTest#testParseTruePref.note: after @prefix true: ..., the object true:o is read as the keyword true followed by :o ("expected . after triple"); longest match makes true:o a PNAME_LN. Subject/predicate position works; object position fails; false: too; turtle12 and trig too.

CustomTurtleParserTest#testSES1988BlankN.spec: RDF 1.2 Turtle section 6.5 [41] BLANK_NODE_LABEL ::= '_:' (PN_CHARS_U | [0-9]) ((PN_CHARS | '.')* PN_CHARS)? and Note 3 (longest match)
CustomTurtleParserTest#testSES1988BlankN.note: in _:blank._:blank the longest BLANK_NODE_LABEL is _:blank._ ('_' is PN_CHARS), leaving :blank with an undeclared empty prefix; RDF4J ends the label before the dot. core rejects, as the grammar requires.

CustomTurtleParserTest#testParsingDefaul.spec: RDF 1.2 Turtle section 7.2 RDF Term Constructors, PNAME_LN: "The namespaces map MUST have a corresponding namespace" (RDF 1.1 Turtle section 7.2 same)
CustomTurtleParserTest#testParsingDefaul.note: RDF4J pre-binds Namespaces.DEFAULT_RDF4J (skos:, rdf:, owl:, ...) by default (BasicParserSettings.NAMESPACES); a document using skos: without @prefix is accepted. core rejects: undefined prefix.

TurtleParserTest#testUnparsableIRIFatal.spec: RDF 1.2 Turtle 7.2 (IRIREF: "The resulting IRI MUST comply with the syntactic restrictions of generic IRI syntax"); RDF 1.2 Concepts 3.3 (an IRI "is a string that conforms to the syntax defined in RFC 3987"); RFC 3987 2.2 (iauthority = [ iuserinfo "@" ] ihost [ ":" port ], port = *DIGIT)
TurtleParserTest#testUnparsableIRIFatal.note: <http://www:example.org/> has a non-digit port, so it is not an IRI under RFC 3987 generic syntax; core accepts it (also in N-Triples). RDF4J rejects (ParsedIRI).

TurtleParserTest#testUnparsableIRINonFat.spec: RDF 1.2 Turtle 7.2 (IRIREF: "The resulting IRI MUST comply with the syntactic restrictions of generic IRI syntax"); RFC 3987 2.2
TurtleParserTest#testUnparsableIRINonFat.note: lenient parse keeps the statement with <http://www:example.org/> (2 quads); RDF4J drops it (1 quad). Same root cause as testUnparsableIRIFatal.

TurtleParserTest#testDirLangStringNoLang.spec: RDF 1.2 Turtle 7.2 (PNAME_LN: "The namespaces map MUST have a corresponding namespace"); RDF 1.2 Concepts 3.4 ("If and only if the datatype IRI is ...rdf:dirLangString, there is a base direction"; likewise a language tag)
TurtleParserTest#testDirLangStringNoLang.note: the input uses rdf: without declaring it; RDF4J's default NAMESPACES setting (RDFa 1.1 initial context plus others) predeclares it, core rejects (undefined prefix). RDF4J also turns "Hello"^^rdf:dirLangString (no language tag) into an xsd:string literal, which the Turtle term constructor (datatype taken from the iri) does not do.
